svg.title: Suez Canal Tactical Cross-Section: The Bar-Lev Sand Rampart, Soviet SAM Umbrella and 1973 Water-Cannon Breach (1969–1973)
svg.desc: West-to-East military engineering cross-section of the Suez Canal front showing Egyptian mobile Soviet SA-2 and SA-3 anti-aircraft missile batteries projecting a 20 km SAM umbrella across the 200 m canal, high-pressure water pumps breaching the 20–25 m 45-degree Israeli sand rampart on 6 October 1973, and a fortified Bar-Lev concrete and rail-timber bunker on the Sinai crest.
svg.text: TACTICAL ENGINEERING CROSS-SECTION · SUEZ CANAL FRONT (1969–1973)
The Bar-Lev Sand Rampart, the Soviet SAM Umbrella & the 1973 Water-Cannon Breach
◀ WEST BANK · EGYPT (SAM Shield & Crossing Staging)

g.text: 20 km SOVIET ANTI-AIRCRAFT "SAM UMBRELLA" (SA-2 & SA-3 DOME)
Pushed to the canal bank in 1970; denied Israeli jets low-level air superiority over the 1973 crossing
• Linked to tactical SA-6 & SA-7 units
• Pump teams drew water straight from
the canal to liquefy the sand wall

svg.text: 1969–1970 WAR OF ATTRITION: ARTILLERY & AIR STALEMATE
• Egyptian artillery barrages failed to demolish the sand-cushioned Bar-Lev
strongpoints, while high explosives merely shifted loose sand back into craters.
• Advancing Soviet SA-2/SA-3 batteries blunted Israeli air raids, freezing the front.
• Bypassing explosives, Egyptian engineers deployed high-pressure water pumps
to carve 81 breaches, washing away 3 million m³ of sand within hours.
• Armoured divisions crossed on pontoon bridges beneath the 20 km SAM shield.
